new_statements.quote: Some of the languages have five-vowel systems, others have seven-vowel systems. Except for group (60), tone is often the only feature distinguishing tenses. Nyekyosa (31) is peculiar in that it makes no use of tone at all. The languages of Zone M are now listed. (10) Fipa-Mambwe Group (11) Pimbwe (Icipimbwe), 8,000 speakers. (12) Rungwa (Icirungwa) 5,000 speakers. (13) Fipa (Icifipa), 78,000 speakers.

sources.citation: Weiss, Jonathan. 2023. A Description of Pimbwe (Bantu, Tanzania): Phonology, Grammar, and Discourse. SIL e-Books 84. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Pimbwe, not Rungwa. On Rungwa it only relays Roth (2011): Rungwa is Pimbwe's closest relative (88% lexical similarity), a five-vowel language, lacks k-lenition, shows spirantization (p.5). Conclusion: 'a comparative study of Pimbwe and Rungwa phonology as well as a Rungwa grammar would doubtless shed light on the Pimbwe language' -- i.e. no Rungwa grammar exists as of 2023. Nothing on Rungwa stress (and no stress statement even for Pimbwe).

sources.citation: embrace_wtz / embracekenya (Wycliffe Associates, Bible Translation Tools / MAST). 2022-2025. Rungwa [rnw] New Testament book drafts (Mark, 1-3 John, 1-2 Peter, 1-2 Thessalonians, 1-2 Timothy, 2 Corinthians, Ephesians, Galatians, James, Jude, Philemon, Philippians, Titus): BTT-Writer 'text/reg' projects translated from the Swahili ULB, hosted on the WACS content server (19 repositories, e.g. embrace_wtz/rnw_mrk_text_reg, 286 chunks, updated 2024-02-26).
sources.note: Nothing: these are community translation drafts with no linguistic front matter. The practical orthography used is plain Latin script with no tone, accent or length diacritics (0 non-ASCII characters in 3,571 characters sampled from Mark 1, 5, 9 and 14; vowel length occasionally written double, e.g. 'Izwii', 'uukii'), so the texts carry no prosodic information. Value: the only running text in Rungwa found anywhere (c. 19 NT books), usable as primary data; evidence that a working Rungwa orthography exists (cf. the SIL Katavi-cluster workshop pointer, A's work 4), though this MAST project is a…
